headline: Ferry Fire Off Coron Leaves at Least 5 Dead as Search Continues
seoTitle: Ferry Fire Off Coron Leaves at Least 5 Dead; Search Continues | FMB News
seoDescription: At least five people died after MV June Aster caught fire off Coron, Palawan. Search and rescue operations continue and preliminary totals may change.
deck: At least five people have died after the passenger ferry MV June Aster caught fire off Coron, Palawan, while rescuers continue searching for people still unaccounted for.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: At least five people were confirmed dead after the passenger ferry MV June Aster caught fire on the evening of September 9 in waters off Coron, Palawan, according to the Philippine Coast Guard and multiple news organizations reporting the Coast Guard's latest updates.

The vessel's manifest listed 117 passengers and 17 crew members, or 134 people in total. Rescue figures were still changing Thursday morning: AP and DZRH reported 42 people rescued, while Reuters later reported 43 rescued. Because search and rescue operations are continuing, FMB News is not treating either rescue or missing-person count as final.

The Coast Guard said the ferry had departed from Manila and was bound for Coron when the fire broke out. Earlier local reporting placed the incident near Barangay Marcilla in Coron. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Philippine Coast Guard deployed personnel and vessels to the area and coordinated with local disaster responders, fire personnel and other maritime units. Search operations continued into Thursday morning despite poor weather, strong waves and currents reported in the area.
Authorities have also said they are monitoring the area for possible pollution while investigators work to determine how the fire started. No verified cause has been announced as of this report.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Inter-island ferries are essential transportation in the Philippines, especially for communities and tourism-dependent areas separated by long sea routes. A casualty incident involving a regularly operating passenger vessel raises immediate questions about emergency response, passenger accounting, fire safety and vessel inspection.

For families of those on board, the most urgent issue is the continuing search and the reconciliation of the passenger manifest with survivors, fatalities and people still unaccounted for. The changing numbers make careful reporting especially important.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The final number of survivors, fatalities and people missing has not yet been established. Rescue totals reported by credible news organizations differ by one person as the operation continues.

The cause and point of origin of the fire remain under investigation. Authorities have not yet released a verified finding on whether mechanical failure, electrical failure, cargo, fuel, weather or another factor caused the blaze.

FMB News will also watch for a reconciled passenger list, official identification of casualties, any confirmed oil spill or environmental impact, and findings from the Coast Guard and Maritime Industry Authority.

sections.heading: Reader note
paragraphs: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

audit.socialCaption: DEVELOPING: At least five people have died after passenger ferry MV June Aster caught fire off Coron, Palawan. Search and rescue operations continue, and preliminary rescue and missing-person totals are still changing. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.
verificationNotes: The central event and at least five confirmed fatalities are corroborated by Reuters, AP, GMA News and DZRH, all citing the Philippine Coast Guard or its spokesperson.
The manifest total of 134 people, composed of 117 passengers and 17 crew members, is consistently reported by Reuters, AP and DZRH based on Coast Guard information.

Credible sources differ on the preliminary rescue count: AP and DZRH reported 42 rescued, while Reuters reported 43. The article discloses this discrepancy and avoids presenting a derived missing-person total as final.
The cause of the fire is explicitly described as under investigation. No theory of causation is presented as fact.

Repository inspection found no September 10 FMB News article before publication and the latest prior repository publications concerned unrelated September 9 stories, so this is treated as an original report rather than a continuation.
The hero and social crops are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved FMB icon and purple-violet/plum treatment. They do not fabricate or imitate documentary photography.
